title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals: Priority Setting Targets for Unpaid Claimants
content:
**Directive — Unemployment Insurance Appeals.** The first-setting target is the number of calendar days, counted from the day the first-setting clock starts, at which an appeal's first hearing date falls. It depends on who appealed and, for a claimant appellant, on what the appealed claim (an Unemployment Benefit Claims record) shows over the two months before today: the benefit payments issued on it and the weeks the claimant certified on it.

**Rule.** The first-setting target is the expedited target days for a claimant appellant on whose appealed claim no benefit payment was issued in the two months before today and who certified at least the expedite minimum weeks on that claim in those two months; it is the priority target days for a claimant appellant on whose appealed claim no benefit payment was issued in those two months and who certified fewer than the expedite minimum weeks on that claim in them; and it is the docket's scheduling target days for an employer appellant and for a claimant appellant on whose appealed claim a benefit payment was issued in those two months. The two months before today cover the dates later than the same day of the month two months before today, up to and including today.

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Expedited target | 14 calendar days |
| Priority target | 18 calendar days |
| Expedite minimum | 3 certified weeks |

## The target as a table

| Appellant | Benefit payment issued on the appealed claim in the two months | Weeks certified on that claim in the two months | First-setting target |
|---|---|---|---|
| claimant | none | 3 or more | 14 days |
| claimant | none | fewer than 3 (including none) | 18 days |
| claimant | one or more | any number | the docket's scheduling target |
| employer | — | — | the docket's scheduling target |

The docket's scheduling target days are: Lower Authority Appeal — Separation Issue 30; Lower Authority Appeal — Able and Available Issue 21; Lower Authority Appeal — Monetary Determination 30; Lower Authority Appeal — Overpayment and Fraud 30; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Benefit Charge 45; Lower Authority Appeal — Employer Contribution Rate 60; Higher Authority Appeal — Board of Review 0 (no hearing).

## Questions answered

- *What counts as a benefit payment issued?* An entry on the appealed claim's payment history recording a benefit payment issued, dated within the two months. Payments on any other claim of the same claimant do not count.
- *What counts as a week certified?* Each weekly certification recorded on the appealed claim with a certification date within the two months.
- *Where do the two months begin?* For today Wednesday 15 April 2026 (hypothetical), the same day two months before is 15 February; the two months cover 16 February through 15 April, both included. A payment issued on 16 February counts; one issued on 15 February does not.
- *Boundary on the weeks (hypothetical claimant, no payment in the two months).* Exactly 3 weeks certified gives 14 days; 2 weeks certified gives 18 days.
- *A claimant was paid once in the window and certified 6 weeks.* A payment was issued, so the target is the docket's scheduling target — 30 days on the Separation Issue docket.
